pages.text: INPUT reads a value into a variable.$(br2)A LABEL with the variable follows, without $(1);$(). The variable must be declared and must be changeable, so a CONSTANT doesn't work. An element works too, like $(1)INPUT names[1]$().

The cursor first looks into the bound I/O blocks. It takes a variable or constant item with the same name and type, or a literal item of the right type. Otherwise it waits until a player types a line on a bound laptop or tablet.
Craft a NOOP block and a tripwire hook together.
Bind a laptop to the function $(1)ask$() and start it. The laptop asks for $(1)count$(). Type 21 and press Enter: the screen shows 42.
$(1)PROGRAM typing$(br)NOOP$(br)NOOP$(br)FUNCTION ask$(br)BEGIN$(br)  VARIABLE count INTEGER$(br)  INPUT count$(br)  PRINT count * 2 ;$(br)END FUNCTION$()
